==Problem==
Ike and Mike go into a sandwich shop with a total of <imath>\$30.00</imath> to spend. Sandwiches cost <imath>\$4.50</imath> each and soft drinks cost <imath>\$1.00</imath> each. Ike and Mike plan to buy as many sandwiches as they can,
and use any remaining money to buy soft drinks. Counting both sandwiches and soft drinks, how
many items will they buy?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }6\qquad\textbf{(B) }7\qquad\textbf{(C) }8\qquad\textbf{(D) }9\qquad\textbf{(E) }10</imath>

== Solution 1 ==
We know that the sandwiches cost <imath>4.50</imath> dollars. Guessing will bring us to multiplying <imath>4.50</imath> by 6, which gives us <imath>27.00</imath>. Since they can spend <imath>30.00</imath> they have <imath>3</imath> dollars left. Since soft drinks cost <imath>1.00</imath> dollar each, they can buy 3 soft drinks, which makes them spend <imath>30.00</imath>  Since they bought 6 sandwiches and 3 soft drinks, they bought a total of <imath>9</imath> items. Therefore, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) }9}</imath>.

- SBose

== Solution 2 (Using Algebra) ==
Let <imath>s</imath> be the number of sandwiches and <imath>d</imath> be the number of sodas. We have to satisfy the equation of
<cmath>4.50s+d=30</cmath>
In the question, it states that Ike and Mike buys as many sandwiches as possible. 
So, we drop the number of sodas for a while.
We have: 
<cmath>\begin{align*}
4.50s&=30 \\
s&=\frac{30}{4.5} \\
s&=6R3
\end{align*}</cmath>
We don't want a remainder so the maximum number of sandwiches is <imath>6</imath>.
The total money spent is <imath>6\cdot 4.50=27</imath>.
The number of dollar left to spent on sodas is <imath>30-27=3</imath> dollars.
<imath>3</imath> dollars can buy <imath>3</imath> sodas leading us to a total of 
<imath>6+3=9</imath> items. 
Hence, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) }9}</imath>.

- by interactivemath

== Solution 3 ==
If the two could by fractions of sandwiches, they'd be able to buy <imath>\frac{30.00\text{ dollars}}{4.50\frac{\text{dollars}}{\text{sandwich}}}=6\frac{2}{3}</imath> sandwiches. But they can only buy a whole number of sandwiches, so they can buy <imath>6</imath>, which costs <imath>6\cdot\$4.50=\$27</imath>. So they have <imath>\$3</imath> left over, from which they can buy <imath>3</imath> drinks (since they each cost <imath>\$1</imath>, for a total item count of <imath>6+3=9</imath> items. The answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}}</imath>

-Elihemi
